title: Lease-windowed burst controller with graceful response degradation
creator: Priya Singh
description: Problem: During sudden tenant bursts and region-level degradation we currently rely on static token buckets + coarse priority lanes. This leads to either: (a) long tail latency for medium-priority tenants, or (b) wholesale circuit-breaker tripping that causes client error spikes. Goals: design and implement a lease-windowed burst controller that hands out short-lived "leases" giving capacity in a sliding window, integrate with our admission controller and circuit breaker layer, and provide graceful response degradation modes (token trimming, partial-response, fallback-model) rather than hard rejection. The controller should: 1) enforce tenant fairness over a configurable sliding window, 2) allow short bursts via lease coupons with backoff when exhausted, 3) surface precise telemetry for SLO attribution, and 4) be compatible with multi-region failover (lease state should degrade gracefully when cross-region coordination is unavailable).
acceptance_criteria: Controller grants leases per tenant with configurable burst size and lease TTL; leases are verifiable and revocable
Under a 5x traffic spike synthetic test, high-priority tenants maintain >= 99.5% of baseline p95 latency while medium tenants experience bounded degradation per policy
No single tenant can consume > configured share over the sliding window; enforcement verified by stress test harness
Integration with circuit breakers: when upstream model pools are unhealthy, controller transitions to defined graceful modes (trim, partial_response, fallback) without tripping global breaker
Telemetry: per-tenant lease issuance, lease exhaustion events, degradation-mode activation events, and SLO delta metrics shipped to observability pipeline
Rollout toggle available in console with canary percent, auto-fallback to legacy token-bucket behavior if rollout errors occur
test_plan: Unit: lease allocator state machine coverage, revocation and TTL expiry paths
Integration: synthetic tenants (500 tenants) run against canary runtime with controlled spike generator; measure per-tenant SLO deltas
Chaos: simulate region partition where cross-region lease sync fails and observe fallback semantics
Performance: ensure lease checks add <500us median to request admission on p4d-like hardware
E2E: enable canary in staging for 48h, verify telemetry and rollback behavior
rollout_plan: 1) Feature gated flag in runtime; default off
2) Canary enable for internal test tenants (5%) for 24h
3) Expand to external dev customers (25%) for 72h with close monitoring
4) Promote to 100% if no regressions; otherwise rollback to legacy token-bucket
5) Post-rollout follow-up: collect 2 weeks of SLO deltas and run parameter tuning job
monitoring: SLO delta dashboard per-tenant and aggregate: p50/p95/p99 latency and error rate delta vs baseline
Alert: surge of lease_exhausted_total > threshold AND overall error_rate increase -> page oncall
Audit logs: record lease grants and revocations tied to request IDs for troubleshooting
implementation_notes: Leases are lightweight signed tokens (HMAC) to avoid cross-region coordination for happy-path validation
Central lease authority (for stronger guarantees) exists as an opt-in mode; default is local-window enforcement with probabilistic reconciliation
Graceful degradation modes prioritized: 1) token trimming (truncate long prompts), 2) partial_response (return condensed summary), 3) fallback_model (cheaper smaller model), 4) hard reject
Circuit breaker integration: breakers subscribe to degradation-mode signals to avoid double-counting failures
Security: leases include tenant ID, sequence, TTL; rotate signing keys via KMS integration

notes_for_ops: Operators can inspect active leases via /admin/leases?tenant=... endpoint (read-only)
In partitioned region, controller will operate in degraded local-mode and emit 'lease_sync_lost' event; ops should not manually revoke unless directed
Backfill job for lease reconciliation runs every 5m; heavy backfill can be disabled via env var during incident
